turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had about two months of fatigue and a few episodes of lower abdominal pain, and I’m feeling really stressed at work. I’m also very worried I might have cancer and I’d like to discuss getting a diagnostic laparoscopy.
To help me narrow this down safely, could you please share your age and sex assigned at birth?

I’m 26 years old, and I was assigned female at birth. I’ve been feeling very tired for about two months and having a few episodes of lower abdominal pain, and I’m quite stressed from work. I’m mainly worried about cancer and would like to discuss whether a diagnostic laparoscopy is appropriate.
Thank you for sharing that. To help narrow this down safely, does the pain tend to occur or worsen around the time of your menstrual period?

“Not really sure—it doesn’t seem clearly tied to my period, and the pain has come in a few separate episodes rather than following my cycle. I’ve mainly just felt persistent fatigue and increased stress, and the cancer worry is driving me to want a laparoscopy to be sure.”
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual bleeding, such as heavier flow, spotting between periods, or unusually painful periods?

“Most of my cycles have been pretty much the same—no heavier bleeding, no spotting between periods, and my periods aren’t unusually painful.” “I’ve mainly had persistent fatigue and those intermittent lower abdominal pain episodes.”
To help distinguish between gastrointestinal and other causes, have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea, constipation, or blood in your stool?
“I haven’t noticed any diarrhea or constipation changes, and I don’t have blood in my stool. Mostly it’s been persistent fatigue with a few intermittent lower abdominal pain episodes.”
Is there any possibility you could be pregnant, or have you taken a pregnancy test recently?

“I’m not sure if there’s any possibility of pregnancy, but I haven’t been able to rule it out yet—I haven’t taken a pregnancy test recently. Given the lower abdominal pain, I can get one done today if you recommend it.”
Have you had any urinary symptoms, such as burning with urination, increased frequency, or urgency?

“I haven’t noticed any burning when I urinate, and no increased frequency or urgency. I’ve mainly just had persistent fatigue and those intermittent lower abdominal pain episodes, plus the stress and concern about cancer.”
Have you experienced any unintentional weight loss, fevers, or drenching night sweats over the past two months?
“No, I don’t think I’ve had any unintentional weight loss, fevers, or night sweats. I mostly feel tired and stressed, and the lower abdominal pain has been intermittent rather than escalating.”
Can you describe exactly where the pain is located (e.g., right side, left side, center, or diffuse) and what it feels like (sharp, dull, crampy, or aching)?

“It’s in the lower abdomen, kind of central but sometimes it feels more on one side than the other; it’s more crampy/aching rather than sharp.” “The episodes come and go, and I’d say they’re mild to moderate—I haven’t had severe, constant pain.”
Are you currently sexually active, and if so, do you use any form of contraception?

Patient: Yes, I’m sexually active, but I use contraception inconsistently, so I can’t reliably say how protected I am. I understand that makes it important to do a pregnancy test and discuss other causes of lower abdominal pain before considering laparoscopy.
Have you noticed any unusual vaginal discharge, odor, or pain during intercourse?

“I haven’t noticed any unusual vaginal discharge or bad odor, and I don’t have pain during intercourse. My main issues have been persistent fatigue and those intermittent, mild-to-moderate crampy lower abdominal pain episodes, along with the stress and my worry about cancer.”
When was the first day of your last menstrual period?

“I’m not entirely sure of the exact first day, but my cycles have been fairly regular and I haven’t noticed any unusual bleeding or spotting—I can check the date on my calendar or apps if that helps.”
Has your most recent period been late, or have you noticed any early pregnancy symptoms like nausea, breast tenderness, or changes in appetite?

Patient: My last period may have been a bit late, but I’m not certain on the dates, and I haven’t had clear early pregnancy symptoms like nausea or breast tenderness—just the ongoing fatigue and intermittent crampy lower abdominal pain. I can take a pregnancy test today if you think it’s the right next step.
[DDX] Early pregnancy (including ectopic pregnancy), Stress-related somatic symptom disorder, Functional ovarian cyst, Pelvic inflammatory disease, Thyroid dysfunction or iron deficiency anemia
